title: ConstructionOS historical governance reconciliation record
description: Schema for records in governance/reconciliations/. One file per reconciled work item, named <WORK-ITEM-ID>.json. A reconciliation is an Architect-owned, ACR-sanctioned overlay for an already-merged work item whose immutable historical ledger contains a specific, enumerated governance defect. It never modifies the original record; it cites the original events verbatim (tamper evidence) and waives exactly the enumerated violations — nothing else. STAGED means the facts are complete but the Architect decision is pending and no waivers are active. DECIDED activates the waivers. The mechanism is owned by ARCH-WF-002; see governance/README.md (Historical governance reconciliation).

work_item.description: The work item whose historical ledger is reconciled. Must be in MERGED or VERIFIED state. Must equal the file name stem.

status.description: STAGED: facts and defect citations complete, Architect decision pending — no waivers are active and the underlying ledger failures remain visible. DECIDED: the Architect decision is recorded and the enumerated waivers are active.

demo.description: true marks a demonstration fixture with synthetic references (a worked example of the mechanism). Demo reconciliations must reference demo work items and demo ACRs.

problem.description: Honest description of the historical defect: what actually happened, with timestamps and commits.

rule.description: The validator rule whose failure is reconciled. Only these three rules are reconcilable, and only for the enumerated violation kinds below — no other failure class can ever be waived.

transition.description: 1-based transition index in the work item's transitions array (matching the validator's human-facing numbering). Required for transition-scoped defects.

state_entry.description: The state being entered for decision-rule defects (e.g. MERGED). Required for rule=decisions.

original.description: The original transition facts, cited verbatim from the work-item record. If the historical record is ever edited, this citation stops matching and the reconciliation fails — tamper evidence.

explanation.description: Why this specific historical violation occurred and why the physical repository history shows the defect was process-recording, not substance.

evidence.description: Evidence the reconciliation decision rests on (the physical git topology, the ledger facts, post-merge verification). Required when DECIDED; each item must be reproducible and revision-bound.

acr.description: The ACR sanctioning this reconciliation. Must exist; must be APPROVED or IMPLEMENTED before the reconciliation may be DECIDED.

decided_by.description: Architect who decided the reconciliation. Required when DECIDED.

rationale.description: The Architect's determination: why the historical record is accepted as reconciled.

remediation.description: What the reconciliation requires or concludes (e.g. the item may proceed to VERIFIED only through the normal architect-verified path).
